title: If they react…
intro: Common reactions in any difficult conversation, and what you could do.

reactions.youCould: Pause. Offer water, tissues or a break. "Take your time." Ask whether they'd like to continue or reschedule. Show empathy, but don't drop the message.

Stay calm and don't match their tone. Acknowledge it: "I can see you're frustrated." Restate the purpose of the meeting. If it escalates, pause and reschedule. You never have to tolerate abuse or threats.
Allow the silence. Ask an open question: "What are you thinking?" Offer time to reflect and agree when you'll follow up.
Listen to their account and ask for specifics. Refer back to the facts. Don't argue. Note the disagreement in the summary.

reactions.ifThey: Raise something new (e.g. a grievance, health or personal issue)
reactions.youCould: Take it seriously. It's fine to pause the original topic. Agree what happens next and contact HR if needed.

reactions.ifThey: Ask for someone to be with them
reactions.youCould: For informal conversations there's usually no legal right to be accompanied, but consider it. For formal disciplinary or grievance hearings, there is a statutory right. Contact HR.
